2026 at 4:12 PM PDT Facebook Twitter LinkedIn Email Listen • 4:56 Igor Ivanko / AFP via Getty Images Diners sit at an outdoor restaurant in Sevastopol, Crimea, on July 22. Ukrainian drone strikes are causing power outages, fuel shortages and cuts in cellphone service in the peninsula. Russia seized Crimea when it first invaded Ukraine in 2014, but now its hold on the territory is being challenged. Russia maintained an iron grip on Crimea since seizing it from Ukraine in 2014. Many Russian civilians go there to enjoy the beaches. But now Ukraine is hitting Crimea hard, upending daily life. KYIV, Ukraine — The Black Sea peninsula of Crimea is normally packed in the summer with families enjoying beach vacations. But not this year, as Ukraine's relentless drone strikes make life increasingly miserable.

"Transportation is completely at a standstill. No gasoline, no fuel, no power. The stores are closed. The banks are closed. Nothing works at all. There's no water either," a Russian woman said on social media .

Crimea was the first place Russian leader Vladimir Putin seized when he initially invaded Ukraine in 2014. An estimated 1 million Russian troops and civilians have poured into the territory to make it more Russian and less Ukrainian. With the Russian influx, and the departure of many Ukrainians, Crimea's population is now estimated at around 2.5 million.
Ukraine has vowed to get Crimea back and carried out periodic drone strikes in recent years, with limited effect. But the campaign has ramped up dramatically in the past couple months.

Russian military facilities have been hit hard, especially in the northern part of Crimea. For civilians, a critical shortage of basic services keeps getting worse in a place that relies heavily on imports.

Prefer the Guardian on Google A Russian military officer labelled as a Ukrainian defector ⁠was killed in a ⁠bomb ​attack on Thursday in Russian-annexed Crimea. Robert Shageyev was described on Russian Telegram channels as ‌a former Ukrainian naval officer who switched allegiance to ‌Russia during Moscow’s annexation of Crimea in 2014 when he was commanding Ukraine’s only submarine, the Zaporizhzhia . Myrotvorets – a Ukrainian website keeping a database of people described as war criminals or ‌traitors – said Shageyev had been “liquidated”.

The attack took place in Sevastopol, the biggest city in Russian-annexed Crimea. ​The regional governor, Mikhail Razvozhayev, said a woman was arrested on suspicion of ⁠assassinating Shageyev on behalf of Ukrainian special services. State news agency TASS quoted the FSB security service as saying the arrested woman was ⁠a Russian national. There was no immediate comment ⁠from Ukraine. Separately, Razvozhayev said four Russian explosives experts and a security guard were killed in Sevastopol while trying to dispose of an explosive device.

A Russian drone attack on a passenger train killed two people , Ukrainian officials said. “Today in the Odesa region, the Russians once again destroyed an ordinary passenger train locomotive with a jet-powered drone. There were 340 people on the train,” said the Ukrainian president, Volodymyr Zelenskyy, on Thursday. “Whoever was operating that drone certainly could not have been unaware that the target was entirely civilian,” he added. The dead were the train’s engineer and assistant engineer, officials said.

article.title: Occupier attacks against Palestinians in West Bank causing ‘serious’ damage to Israel: Report
article.description: Security officials warn violence against Palestinians inflicting political damage, straining Israeli forces deployed in territory | Anadolu
paragraphs: WORLD TÜRKİYE ECONOMY POLITICS ENERGY TECHNOLOGY US-Iran war Hormuz crisis Russia-Ukraine war EDITION Türkçe English BHSC Pусский Français العربية Kurdî کوردی Shqip فارسی македонски Bahasa Indonesia Español Middle East Occupier attacks against Palestinians in West Bank causing ‘serious’ damage to Israel: Report Security officials warn violence against Palestinians inflicting political damage, straining Israeli forces deployed in territory Said Amori and Mohammad Sio 22 August 2026 • Update : 22 August 2026 JERUSALEM/ISTANBUL Israeli security officials have warned that attacks by occupiers against Palestinians in the West Bank are causing “serious” political damage to Israel, public broadcaster KAN reported Friday.

The officials, who were not identified, said soldiers are being forced to deal with incidents on the ground amid “a lack of firm law enforcement by police and other state authorities, in some cases without adequate tools or sufficient support.”

The attacks are “taking place before the eyes of the entire world and causing serious political damage to Israel,” said officials, adding that they are also placing a strain on Israeli forces deployed in the West Bank.
The criticism followed an occupier attack Friday on the West Bank town of Sa’ir, in Hebron province, that killed Karim Shalaldeh, 17, and wounded others.

The Israeli army said a group of occupiers entered the town on a “trip” without prior coordination with the military and claimed they came under stone-throwing by Palestinians, according to the broadcaster.

Israeli military raids and attacks by Israelis from illegal settlements across the occupied West Bank have injured at least 19 Palestinians, according to Palestinian health officials and local media reports.
Israeli forces shot and injured three Palestinians who attempted to enter occupied East Jerusalem near the separation wall in ar-Ram, the Jerusalem Governorate said on Saturday.
It said the incident was part of near-daily attacks against Palestinian workers barred from their jobs in Israel since the genocidal war on Gaza began in October 2023.

In the Tubas Governorate in northern West Bank, the Palestine Red Crescent Society said its crews treated at least 11 Palestinians, including four children, for tear gas inhalation during Israeli army raids.

In Masafer Yatta, south of Hebron, an elderly man was beaten and bruised by armed settlers, after which Israeli forces raided his home, damaged its contents and confiscated his family’s phones, the Palestinian news agency Wafa reported.

article.title: Tear gas shelling, detentions, property theft reported during West Bank raids
paragraphs: Israeli settlers and the military have continued raids in the occupied West Bank, including the one in which eleven 11 Palestinians, four children among them, suffered from suffocation caused by tear smoke inhalation.

* Wafa reported that during an Israeli military raid on the city of Tubas and the village of Tayasir, east of the city, 11 residents suffered suffocation due to inhalation of tear gas smoke. They were treated by Palestine Red Crescent crews.
* Israeli settlers stole Palestinian property from a Palestinian community near the village of Abu Falah, northeast of Ramallah in the occupied West Bank, according to the Quds News Network.
* Israeli forces stormed the city of Qalqilya, according to QNN.

* A large Israeli military force surrounded the Thabet Roundabout in central Tulkarm on Saturday night, amid heavy gunfire and the firing of stun and illumination grenades, Wafa reported. During the raid, Israeli forces detained a young man whose identity was not immediately known.

They also set fire to a vehicle, partially burning it, and spray-painted racist slogans at the site, the sources said.

Meanwhile, in Bethlehem, Israeli occupiers attacked the Khala’il al-Louz area east of the city, damaging irrigation pipes used for crops, cutting down trees and damaging Palestinian property and agricultural land.
Israeli occupiers also uprooted olive and grape trees from Palestinian-owned land in al-Minya village, east of Bethlehem, according to the official Palestinian news agency Wafa.
In Nablus, Israeli forces raided the towns of Beita, Tell and Beit Dajan, storming and searching several homes, Wafa reported.
